stem: Under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, when must an employee with occupational exposure receive bloodborne-pathogen training?

options.A: Only once, before the employee's first shift
options.B: At initial assignment, at least annually thereafter, and additionally when task or procedure changes affect occupational exposure
options.C: Only after an exposure incident occurs
options.D: Only when the employee requests training

rationale: OSHA requires bloodborne-pathogen training at the time of initial assignment to tasks with occupational exposure, at least annually thereafter, and additional training when changes in tasks or procedures affect exposure.
educational_objective: Identify OSHA-required timing for bloodborne-pathogen training.
source_claim_supported: Employees with occupational exposure require training at initial assignment, at least annually, and when task/procedure changes alter exposure.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — occupational exposure prevention
correction_summary: Used the exact federal training-timing provisions and removed unsupported institutional variations.
